# Fairstay MCO Contracts (`fairstay-mco-contracts`)

Managed care contract review for nursing homes: claims paid below the contract rate, per-diems below your benchmark, contracts ended or in their notice window, rates unchanged for years, plans paying with no contract on file, and a payer matrix for the admissions team. Resident names and claim numbers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay MCO Contracts never sends a termination, renewal or dispute notice to a plan.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Managed care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-mco-contracts demo
npx -y fairstay-mco-contracts mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional managed care contracts for Cedar Hollow, reviewed on 1 April 2026. Planted:

- Lone Star Health Advantage paid 14 Level 3 days at 650 a day against a 700 contract rate (700 short).
- The Prairie Star Plus Medicaid managed care contract ended 28 February 2026 and does not renew on its own.
- Hill Country Health paid a claim and has no contract on file.
- Gulf Coast HMO renews on 30 June unless notice is given by 1 May. Its Level 1 and Level 2 rates are 45 and 60 a day below the benchmark and have not changed since July 2023.
- Bluebonnet Care Plan paid exactly its contract rate.

Resident names and claim numbers are in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells `benchmarks`, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `mco_check` | Review contract rates, dates and payments, and build the payer matrix. | runs |
| `mco_payer_matrix` | The payer matrix for admissions: each plan, level, rate, benchmark and whether the contract is in force. | runs |
| `mco_write_report` | Write mco-contracts.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and mco-contracts.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/mco). | runs |
| `mco_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `mco_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `mco_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `mco_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `contract_notice_send` | Fairstay MCO Contracts never sends a termination, renewal or dispute notice to a plan. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `mco_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `contracts` (required) | Managed care contracts under --root: payer, plan, level, per-diem rate, start, end, auto renew, notice days, last rate change |
| `payments` | Optional remittance lines: payer, level, resident, claim, from date, days, paid |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: benchmarks, warn_days, stale_years |
| `as_of` | Review date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-mco-contracts inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Managed care contracts (`contracts`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `plan` | text | Plan, Product, Plan Name, Line of Business |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `rate` (required) | amount | Rate, Per Diem, Daily Rate, Contract Rate |
| `start` | date | Start, Effective, Effective Date, Start Date |
| `end` | date | End, Term End, End Date, Expires, Expiration |
| `auto_renew` | text | Auto Renew, Fairstay, Renews, Auto-Renew |
| `notice_days` | number | Notice Days, Notice, Termination Notice Days |
| `last_rate_change` | date | Last Rate Change, Rate Changed, Last Increase |

### Remittance lines (`payments`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `claim_id` | text (masked) | Claim, Claim ID, Claim Number, ICN |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Service From, From Date, Start |
| `days` (required) | number | Days, Units, Covered Days |
| `paid` (required) | amount | Paid, Paid Amount, Payment, Amount |

## Settings file (`mco_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `benchmarks` | Your market or cost benchmark per level: [{level, rate}] (a row with no level covers the rest) |
| `warn_days` | Flag notice dates and ends within this many days (default 30) |
| `stale_years` | Flag rates unchanged for longer than this (default 2 years) |

## Memory

`mco_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `mco_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `plan_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-mco-contracts": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-mco-contracts",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-mco-contracts -- npx -y fairstay-mco-contracts mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-mco-contracts tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-mco-contracts sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-mco-contracts inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-mco-contracts call mco_check '{"contracts":"<contracts>"}'
fairstay-mco-contracts eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-mco-contracts demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
